summary: A list of the UCLA Campus Computing Network contacts for ARPANET users, including user relations, ARPA liaison, the technical liaison, operations and consulting. It tells users whom to contact first. It was replaced by RFC 423.

plainLanguage.summary: A who-to-call list for a computer center at UCLA, saying which person to ask for each kind of problem.

subtitle: Contact information for UCLA's ARPANET network liaison staff.

tldr.problem: ARPANET users needed to know whom to contact at UCLA Campus Computing Network for different types of assistance.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists the names, titles and phone numbers of six staff members responsible for user relations, technical liaison, operations and consulting.
tldr.outcome: This helped users reach the right person for administrative matters, technical problems or operational support.

today: RFC 389 is a historic reference. It was superseded by RFC 423.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: This RFC publishes contact information for the staff at UCLA's Campus Computing Network (CCN) who support ARPANET users. Six staff members are listed with their titles, responsibilities and phone numbers.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a who-to-call list for a computer center.

sections.title: Contact Points
sections.content: The RFC identifies three main contact points. Fred Ebrahimi (User Relations) handles administrative matters such as charge numbers and funding. Robert Braden (Network Technical Liaison) handles problems with network protocol and hardware. Barbara Noble (User Services) is the focal point for programming problems and site usage issues, and can also route calls to the consulting desk or the operations manager.
sections.plainLanguage: Fred helps with money and account setup. Bob fixes network problems. Barbara helps with programming and other problems while you are using the system.

sections.title: Operational Support
sections.content: For operational matters such as schedules and special handling, users should contact the Operations desk or William Tippit, the Operations Manager.
sections.plainLanguage: The operations desk tells you when the system will be down and handles special requests.
